people.name: Patrick McKeown
people.role: Buteyko Instructor — CO₂ Tolerance and Nasal Breathing
people.key_contribution: Popularized Buteyko method for asthma and athletic performance globally; developed BOLT score (Body Oxygen Level Test) as CO₂ tolerance metric; authored 'The Oxygen Advantage'; helped generate clinical interest in nasal breathing science

people.name: Wim Hof
people.key_contribution: PNAS 2014 study (Kox et al.) showed his breathing method can modulate sympathetic NS + suppress innate immune response; raises awareness of breathwork; however, safety record includes drowning deaths from his method — requires safety warnings
notable_works: Kox M et al. PNAS 2014 — 24 trained vs untrained participants

people.name: David Nieman, PhD
people.role: Exercise Immunologist — Exercise and Respiratory Infections
people.key_contribution: Foundational research on exercise and URTI risk (J-curve model: moderate exercise reduces risk, extreme exercise increases it); n=1,002 URTI study; established 'open window' hypothesis for overtraining immune suppression
notable_works: Nieman DC et al. Br J Sports Med 2011 — Exercise and URTI

people.name: Fiona Cowie / Cochrane Breathing Group
people.role: Cochrane Reviewer — Breathing Exercises for Asthma
people.key_contribution: Cochrane systematic review of breathing exercises (Buteyko, Papworth) for asthma; provided balanced evidence assessment showing reduced bronchodilator use but insufficient evidence for spirometric improvement
notable_works: Cowie RL et al. Cochrane 2008 — Breathing exercises for asthma

people.name: Peter Poole / Cochrane Airways Group
people.role: Cochrane Reviewer — Mucolytic Agents for COPD
people.key_contribution: Lead author of multiple Cochrane reviews on mucolytic agents (NAC) for COPD; established 22% exacerbation reduction with NAC/mucolytic treatment; key evidence base for NAC clinical use in COPD
notable_works: Poole P et al. Cochrane 2019 — Mucolytic agents versus placebo for COPD

people.name: Lung Association Thailand / Thai Thoracic Society
people.key_contribution: Local Thai clinical guidelines for asthma and COPD management; context-specific air quality data (PM2.5 in Bangkok, Chiang Mai haze season); recommendations for Thai climate and patient population

molecules.name: Nitric Oxide (NO)
molecules.role_in_domain: Produced in nasal sinuses during nasal breathing; bronchodilator + vasodilator + antimicrobial; explains superior respiratory efficiency of nasal vs mouth breathing; reduced in mouth-breathers

molecules.name: Leukotriene B4 (LTB4)
molecules.role_in_domain: Pro-inflammatory mediator in asthma; recruits eosinophils; targets of leukotriene modifier drugs (montelukast); replaced by anti-inflammatory LTB5 when EPA substitutes arachidonic acid

molecules.name: Mucin
molecules.role_in_domain: Main component of airway mucus; cross-linked by disulfide bonds (viscous thick mucus in COPD/bronchitis); NAC cleaves disulfide bonds → thinner mucus → easier clearance

molecules.name: Neutrophil Elastase
molecules.role_in_domain: Released by neutrophils in COPD pathogenesis; destroys alveolar elastic tissue → emphysema; target of alpha-1 antitrypsin (AAT) naturally; AAT deficiency = genetic COPD cause

molecules.name: PM2.5 (Particulate Matter <2.5 μm)
molecules.role_in_domain: Bypasses mucociliary clearance; reaches alveoli; triggers macrophage activation + ROS + systemic inflammation; independent CVD and lung cancer risk factor; major Thai public health concern

molecules.name: BOLT Score (Body Oxygen Level Test)
molecules.role_in_domain: Measures CO₂ tolerance (seconds before air hunger after exhale); <20s = chronic over-breathing; >40s = good CO₂ tolerance; used in Buteyko training to track progress

molecules.name: IL-5 (Interleukin-5)
molecules.role_in_domain: Recruits and activates eosinophils into airway → asthma inflammation; target of biologic therapies (mepolizumab, reslizumab); elevated by Th2 polarization

molecules.name: Glutathione (GSH)
molecules.role_in_domain: Primary antioxidant in airway epithelium; protects lung cells from PM2.5, cigarette smoke, viral oxidative stress; synthesized from NAC; depleted in COPD and heavy smokers

organizations.name: GOLD (Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease)
organizations.role: Annually updated COPD guidelines; GOLD staging system (GOLD 1-4 by FEV1); standard of care globally; includes pulmonary rehab as standard treatment

organizations.name: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma)
organizations.role: Annually updated asthma guidelines; step therapy protocol (ICS, LABA, biologics); accepted IV Mg for severe acute asthma; reference for all evidence-based asthma claims

organizations.name: WHO Air Quality Division
organizations.role: WHO 2021 Air Quality Guidelines: PM2.5 annual 5 μg/m³ (updated from 10), 24h 15 μg/m³; key reference for PM2.5 health claims

organizations.name: Pollution Control Department Thailand (กรมควบคุมมลพิษ)
organizations.role: Real-time Thailand AQI data; PM2.5 monitoring; Chiang Mai haze season alerts; Thai AQI standards (slightly different from WHO AQI)

case_studies.title: Poole 2019 Cochrane — NAC/Mucolytics for COPD (13 RCTs, n=4,155)
case_studies.description: Meta-analysis of 13 RCTs; primary outcome: COPD exacerbation; NAC 600mg/day reduced exacerbations by 22%; no significant safety concerns at standard doses; authors noted benefit most pronounced in patients not on inhaled corticosteroids; gold standard evidence for NAC in COPD

case_studies.title: Chiang Mai PM2.5 Crisis 2019-2023
case_studies.description: Annual haze season (February-April) from agricultural burning in upper Thailand and neighboring countries; AQI 200-400+ regularly; Chiang Mai ranked among worst global air quality during peaks; significant cardiovascular and respiratory ED admissions increase correlated with PM2.5 spikes; key Thailand-specific context for respiratory health content
case_studies.source: Thai Pollution Control Department annual reports

case_studies.title: Kox 2014 PNAS — Wim Hof Method RCT
case_studies.description: 24 participants (trained Wim Hof method vs untrained); injected with E. coli endotoxin; Wim Hof group showed higher adrenaline, lower cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α), fewer flu-like symptoms; groundbreaking evidence that voluntary breathing technique can modulate sympathetic NS + innate immune response; NOTE: single study, small n, requires replication; safety warnings critical for breathing technique recommendations
